title: Moving the registered office to another city within the same ROC
law: Section 12(5); Rules 25 and 27, Companies (Incorporation) Rules, 2014; Regulations 30, 44 and 46(3), SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015
summary: Moves the registered office from one city, town or village to another while staying under the same Registrar of Companies, using a special resolution and a notice to the Registrar.
when: When the company wants a new registered office outside the local limits of the city, town or village where the present one sits, but within the same ROC area.
applies: All companies; extra stock exchange steps for listed companies

steps.d: Directors approve the shift from the present city to the new city within the same ROC area and State. They approve the draft notice of the general meeting, authorise the CS or another officer to send it, and authorise an officer to sign documents and do the needed acts.

steps.t: Stock exchange intimation of board outcome (listed)
steps.d: A listed company informs each stock exchange of the board decision as soon as reasonably possible, and within the time the reference note gives (24 hours of the meeting). It also posts the same on its website within 2 working days.
Hold a general meeting and pass a special resolution to change the registered office to the new city. Send the notice with an explanatory statement.

steps.t: Stock exchange disclosures of the meeting (listed)
steps.d: Send the proceedings of the general meeting (not for a postal ballot) to the exchanges within 24 hours of the close of the meeting and post them on the website within 2 working days. File the voting results with the exchanges within 2 working days of the meeting and post them on the website.
File a copy of the special resolution with its explanatory statement with the ROC.

steps.t: File notice of change of registered office
steps.d: File the notice and verification of the new registered office with the Registrar, with the prescribed fee. Attach proof of the new premises (title document, or notarised lease with a rent receipt not older than one month, or the owner's authorisation with proof of ownership, or an NOC from the director if the director owns the premises) and a utility bill not older than two months. Also attach the list of other companies using the same premises, with their CIN.
steps.time: Within 30 days of the special resolution (see flags)
docs: Certified true copy of special resolution with explanatory statement
List of other companies at the same address

steps.d: On approval of MGT-14 and INC-22, the Registrar records the new location of the registered office.

steps.t: Tell the stock exchanges the effective date (listed)
steps.d: Inform the exchanges of the date the change takes effect, as soon as reasonably possible and within 24 hours of the Registrar registering the notice. Post it on the website.
Show the new address outside every office or place of business, and on business letters, bill heads, letter papers, notices and other official publications.

Apply to update the address with GST, the Shops and Establishment authority, factories law authority, FEMA/RBI where relevant, inter-state migrant workmen, private security agency, EPF, ESI, other labour laws and any industry-specific regulator.

forms.purpose: Filing of the special resolution with the explanatory statement
Notice of the situation of the registered office and verification
forms.deadline: Within 30 days (reference note: of the special resolution)

checklist: Articles and MOA checked for the registered office clause
Proof of the new premises (title or lease with rent receipt or owner authorisation)
Utility bill for the new address, not older than 2 months
NOC from the director if the director owns the premises
List of other companies at the same address, with CIN
Board resolution and draft notice approved
Special resolution passed and certified copy ready
MGT-14 and INC-22 filed in time
Stock exchange intimations made (listed company)
New address updated on stationery, website, GST and other registrations

resolutions.title: Board approval for shifting the registered office to another city
resolutions.text:
RESOLVED THAT, subject to the approval of the members, the registered office of {co} be shifted from [present address] to [new address], being in [new city] within the jurisdiction of the same Registrar of Companies, [name of ROC], under Section 12(5) of the Companies Act, 2013.
RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the draft notice of the general meeting to be held on [date] at [time] at [venue], with the explanatory statement, is approved and the Company Secretary [name] is authorised to send it to all members, directors and auditors.
RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [name of director / Company Secretary / CFO] is authorised to sign all forms, papers and documents and to do all acts needed to give effect to this resolution.

resolutions.title: Special resolution for shifting the registered office to another city
resolutions.text:
RESOLVED THAT, pursuant to Section 12(5) and other applicable provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 and the rules made under it, the registered office of {co} be shifted from [present address], [old city], to [new address], [new city], within the jurisdiction of the Registrar of Companies, [name of ROC].
RESOLVED FURTHER THAT, to the extent the Memorandum of Association refers to the location of the registered office, it be altered to read as set out in the explanatory statement.
RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [name of director / Company Secretary] is authorised to file e-forms MGT-14 and INC-22 and to do all acts needed to give effect to this resolution.
resolutions.explanatory: The Board proposes to shift the registered office from [old address] to [new address] because [reason, e.g. better access, larger premises, cost]. The new premises are [owned by / taken on lease by / provided by the owner under authorisation to] the Company. Under Section 12(5), a special resolution is needed to move the registered office outside the local limits of the present city, town or village. No director or key managerial person, or their relatives, is interested in this resolution except [state interest, if any]. The Board recommends the resolution for approval.

flags: INC-22 timing: the reference note ties the 30 days to the special resolution. Section 12(4) and Rule 25/27 count 30 days from the date of change of the registered office (and from incorporation for a new company). File within 30 days of the actual change and confirm on the current form.

Listed company timings: the reference note says 24 hours for board outcomes and general meeting proceedings. Under Regulation 30 and Schedule III, board outcomes are generally due within 30 minutes of the meeting close, and other events within 12 or 24 hours. Check the current schedule.

The reference note attaches an 'altered MOA'. A Memorandum usually names only the State in its registered office clause, so no alteration is needed for a move within a State unless the MOA names the city. Check the MOA.

Rule 22(16) of the Management and Administration Rules may require a postal ballot for a change of registered office outside local limits. Verify for the company and whether e-voting at a meeting is accepted.
A move within the same city, town or village needs only a board resolution and INC-22 notice, not a special resolution (Section 12(5) applies only outside local limits).

title: Moving the registered office from one ROC area to another within the same State
summary: Moves the registered office to a place under a different Registrar of Companies in the same State, after the Regional Director confirms the change.
when: When the new office address falls under another ROC area but stays in the same State.

steps.d: Send notice of the board meeting to every director.
steps.time: At least 7 days before the meeting

steps.d: Hold the meeting with a valid quorum. Approve the shift of the registered office and the alteration of the Memorandum. Fix the date, time and place of the extraordinary general meeting.
Send notice with an explanatory statement to all members, all directors and every other person entitled to notice.
steps.time: At least 21 clear days before the meeting

steps.d: Pass a special resolution approving the shift of the registered office and the change to the Memorandum.
File with the ROC a certified true copy of the special resolution and a copy of the meeting notice with its explanatory statement.
docs: Certified true copy of special resolution

steps.d: File the application for confirmation with the fee. Attach the board resolution, the special resolution, a declaration by the KMP or two authorised directors that workmen's dues are paid and creditors have consented or provision is made, a declaration that the company will not seek to change the court jurisdiction for pending prosecutions, and the acknowledged intimation to the Chief Secretary of the State about the shift and that employees' interests are protected.
The Regional Director examines the application, may decide without a hearing, and passes the order approving or rejecting it.
steps.time: Within 15 days of a complete application

steps.t: File the order with the ROC
steps.d: File the certified copy of the Regional Director's order with the Registrar of the State, with the fee.
steps.time: Within 30 days of receiving the certified order
docs: Certified copy of Regional Director's order

steps.t: File notice of the new registered office
steps.d: File the notice with proof of the new address (conveyance deed, or lease or rent agreement with receipts not older than one month), utility bills not older than two months, an NOC from the premises owner, a list of companies at the same address with CIN, the certified special resolution and the Regional Director's order.
steps.time: Within 30 days of the confirming order
docs: List of companies at same address

steps.d: If useful, publish a newspaper notice telling members and others to send communications to the new address.
Show the new address on all records and registers, including the register of members, share certificates, sign boards and name plates.
Apply for the address change under GST, FEMA, EPFO, ESIC, Shops and Establishment, factories law, other labour laws and industry-specific laws.

Application to Regional Director for confirmation of shift
Filing of Regional Director's order with the Registrar
forms.deadline: Within 30 days of receiving the certified order

forms.purpose: Notice of change of registered office
forms.deadline: Within 30 days of the confirming order

RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the Memorandum of Association be altered as needed to reflect the shift, subject to the approval of the members.
RESOLVED FURTHER THAT an extraordinary general meeting be held on [date] at [time] at [venue], and the notice with the explanatory statement is approved.
RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [name of director / KMP] is authorised to sign the declarations, file the e-forms and appear before the Regional Director.

resolutions.title: Special resolution for shifting the registered office to another ROC area in the same State
resolutions.text:
RESOLVED THAT, pursuant to Section 12 and other applicable provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 and Rule 28 of the Companies (Incorporation) Rules, 2014, and subject to the confirmation of the Regional Director, the registered office of {co} be shifted from [present address] to [new address], moving from the jurisdiction of the Registrar of Companies, [old ROC], to that of [new ROC], within the State of [State].
RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the Memorandum of Association be altered to the extent needed to reflect this shift.
RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [name of director / Company Secretary] is authorised to file MGT-14, INC-23, INC-28 and INC-22 and do all acts needed to give effect to this resolution.
resolutions.explanatory: The Board proposes to shift the registered office from [old address] to [new address] because [reason]. The shift moves the Company to another ROC area in the same State and needs a special resolution and the confirmation of the Regional Director. The Company will declare that it has paid its workmen and has the consent of its creditors or has made provision for their payment, and that it will not seek a change in court jurisdiction for pending prosecutions. No director or KMP or their relatives is interested in this resolution except [state interest, if any]. The Board recommends the resolution.

docs.title: Declaration on workmen's dues and creditors
paras: We, [name of KMP / director 1] and [name of director 2], authorised by the Board of {co} (CIN [CIN]), declare that the Company has not defaulted in paying dues to its workmen, and that it has obtained the consent of its creditors for the proposed shift of its registered office from [old address] to [new address], or has made proper provision for payment of their dues.
Date: [date]. Place: [place]. Signed: [name and designation].

docs.title: Declaration on court jurisdiction
paras: {co} (CIN [CIN]) declares that it will not seek any change in the jurisdiction of the Court in which prosecution cases against it or its officers are pending, as a result of the proposed shift of its registered office from [old address] to [new address].
Date: [date]. Place: [place]. Signed: [name and designation].

docs.title: Intimation to the Chief Secretary of the State
paras: To, The Chief Secretary, Government of [State]. Subject: Intimation of proposed shift of registered office of {co}.

The Company proposes to shift its registered office from [old address] to [new address] within the State. The Company confirms that the interests of its employees will not be adversely affected by this shift. A copy of the application to the Regional Director is enclosed.
Yours faithfully, [name and designation].

flags: The Regional Director's 15-day period starts from a complete application, as the reference note says. Check the current form instructions and the Rule 28 text for exact sub-rule timelines.

The reference note cites Sections 12(5) and 12(6). I believe the Regional Director's confirmation under Rule 28 sits under Section 13(4) read with Rule 28, not only Section 12. Verify the section reference before quoting it.

The reference note asks for INC-22 within 30 days of the Regional Director's order, and INC-28 within 30 days of the certified order. Rule 28 may give a different sequence for the Registrar's registration; check the rule and the MCA form version.
The reference note attaches a notice to the Chief Secretary in INC-23. Check whether the current rule still requires this intimation for a shift within the same State.

title: Issuing share certificates after incorporation
law: Section 46(1); Rule 5, Companies (Share Capital and Debentures) Rules, 2014; Section 88; Rule 3, Companies (Management and Administration) Rules, 2014; Section 56(4)(a)
summary: Covers the board approvals, signing, stamping, delivery and register entries needed to give subscribers their share certificates after the company is incorporated.
when: After incorporation, when the subscribers to the Memorandum are to receive certificates for their shares.

steps.d: Confirm that subscribers have paid the subscription money. Authorise allotment according to the number, face value, class and type of shares each subscriber took. Authorise a person to print and safely keep blank certificates in the format of Form SH-1. Authorise two directors, or a director and the company secretary (if any), or another person named by the Board, to sign certificates and to affix the common seal if the company has one.
Affix revenue stamps on the certificates at the rates in the Stamp Act of the State where the registered office is.
Give the share certificates to the subscribers to the Memorandum.
Record the members in the register of members as required by Section 88 in the prescribed format.
steps.time: Within 7 days of allotment (per the reference note)

steps.d: Authorise the company secretary or another person to authenticate entries in the register of members.
The company secretary or the person the Board authorises signs off the entries in the register of members.

forms.purpose: Format of the share certificate (Rule 5)
forms.deadline: Certificates delivered within 2 months of incorporation

checklist: Subscription money received from every subscriber
Board resolution on allotment and certificates passed
Blank certificates printed in SH-1 format and kept safely
Signatories authorised (two directors, or a director and the CS)
Stamp duty paid as per State rules
Certificates delivered within 2 months of incorporation
Register of members completed and authenticated
Details of each certificate entered in the register

resolutions.text:
RESOLVED THAT the Board notes that the subscribers to the Memorandum of {co} have paid the subscription money of Rs. [amount] and that [number] equity shares of Rs. [face value] each are to be recorded in favour of the subscribers as set out in the Memorandum.
RESOLVED FURTHER THAT, under Section 46 of the Companies Act, 2013 and Rule 5 of the Companies (Share Capital and Debentures) Rules, 2014, share certificates in the format of Form SH-1 be issued to the subscribers.
RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [name] is authorised to print and keep the blank certificates safely, and that [name of director 1] and [name of director 2 / Company Secretary] are authorised to sign them and to affix the common seal, if any.

RESOLVED THAT, under Section 88 of the Companies Act, 2013, the entries in the register of members of {co} be authenticated by [name], Company Secretary / [name of authorised person].
RESOLVED FURTHER THAT every future entry in the register be authenticated in the same way.

docs.title: Covering letter for delivery of share certificate
paras: To, [name of subscriber], [address]. Subject: Share certificate no. [number] of {co}.
We enclose share certificate no. [number] for [number] equity shares of Rs. [face value] each, numbered [from] to [to], registered in your name. Please acknowledge receipt.
Yours faithfully, [name and designation], for {co}.

flags: The reference note says to enter the register of members 'in Form MGT-7'. MGT-7 is the annual return. The register of members is kept in Form MGT-1 under Rule 3, so use MGT-1.
The reference note gives 7 days from allotment for the register entry. I cannot match this to a statutory period in Rule 3; check before treating it as a deadline.

Signing rule: Section 46 and Rule 5 call for two directors, one of them the managing director or a whole-time director if there is one, and the company secretary. The reference note allows a director with the company secretary or another authorised person. Check the current text.
Subscribers to the Memorandum become members on incorporation; the 'allotment' step is a record for them and the PAS-3 return does not normally apply to them. Verify for your case.

title: Reducing share capital with NCLT approval
law: Sections 66 and 52; National Company Law Tribunal (Procedure for Reduction of Share Capital of Company) Rules, 2016; for listed companies, SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015
summary: Cuts the company's share capital through a special resolution, a scheme approved by the NCLT, and filings with the Registrar and stock exchanges.
when: When a company wants to cancel lost capital, release unpaid liability on shares, or pay back capital it does not need.
applies: Private, public and listed companies; steps 5, 6, 8, 10, 11, 13, 14, 29, 30, 34 and 38 of the reference note do not apply to private companies

steps.d: See whether the Articles allow a reduction of capital. If not, alter them first to give the power.

Decide how to reduce: remove or lessen liability on unpaid share capital; or, with or without lessening liability, cancel paid-up capital that is lost or not backed by assets; or pay back paid-up capital that is more than the company needs. Then alter the Memorandum to show the reduced capital and shares.

steps.t: Appoint a valuer if paying back capital
steps.d: If the plan is to pay back excess paid-up capital, hold a board meeting or pass a circular resolution to appoint a registered valuer to value the shares and set the payout.

steps.t: Notice of board meeting and stock exchange intimation
steps.d: After the valuation report arrives, send notice of the board meeting. A listed company gives the exchanges at least 2 working days' prior intimation (excluding the intimation day and meeting day) and closes the trading window under its insider trading code, telling the exchanges.
steps.time: Board notice at least 7 days; exchanges 2 working days

steps.d: Hold the meeting or pass a circular resolution to approve the reduction scheme and authorise directors to act, including authorising a practising CS, CA, CMA or advocate to appear before the NCLT. Approve the general meeting notice with the explanatory statement.

Send the board outcome to the exchanges within 30 minutes of the meeting close and post it on the website within 2 working days. Send the draft scheme to the exchanges to get a no objection letter before going to the NCLT. Private companies skip these steps.

Send notice to all members and hold a general meeting to approve the scheme by special resolution (a postal ballot also works). A listed company sends the outcome to the exchanges within 12 hours and the voting results within 2 working days, and posts the outcome on its website within 2 working days.

steps.t: File the resolutions with the ROC
steps.d: File the special resolution with its explanatory statement. The reference note also asks a public or listed company to file the board resolution within 30 days of the board meeting.
steps.time: Within 30 days of the general meeting (board resolution: 30 days of board meeting)

steps.d: After the exchange no objection letter, file the application with fee of Rs. 5,000. Attach: affidavit verifying the petition; creditors' list certified by the MD (or two directors) not earlier than 15 days before filing, with an auditor's certificate that it is correct; auditor's certificate and director declaration that there are no deposit or interest arrears; auditor's certificate that the accounting treatment meets Section 133 standards; papers supporting any dispensation sought on creditor notices; MOA and AOA; audited accounts for the last 3 years; certified board and special resolutions; valuation report; and, as advised, latest accounts made up not earlier than 15 days before filing.
At the same time, keep copies of the list at the registered office for inspection during business hours. Inspection costs Rs. 50 and extracts cost Rs. 10 per page.

The NCLT lists the application for admission. Once admitted, it directs notices seeking objections within 15 days of receiving the application to the Central Government (delegated to the Regional Director), the ROC and, for a listed company, SEBI, all in Form RSC-2, and to creditors in Form RSC-3. Creditor notices go out within 7 days of the NCLT's direction.
steps.time: Creditor notices within 7 days of direction

steps.d: As the NCLT directs, publish the notice in a leading English newspaper and a leading vernacular newspaper, both circulating in the State of the registered office, and upload it to the website. It states the proposed reduction, where the creditors' list can be seen, and the time fixed for objections and the hearing date.
The directors file an affidavit confirming dispatch and publication of the notices.
steps.time: Within 7 days of issuing the notices

steps.d: Objections from creditors, the ROC, the Government or anyone else are filed within 3 months of the publication of the notice; with none, no objection is presumed. The NCLT may dispense with creditor notices or advertisement if every creditor's debt is paid, secured or consented. The company then sends the objections with its replies to the NCLT.
steps.time: Replies within 7 days after the objection period ends

steps.d: The NCLT hears the case, may order enquiries or security for non-consenting creditors, and passes an order confirming the reduction, with any terms. A listed company discloses the final hearing outcome within 24 hours and posts it on its website within 2 working days, and files any documents the exchanges or SEBI require.

steps.t: File the order and get the certificate
steps.d: File the NCLT order with the ROC. The ROC registers it and issues a certificate.
steps.time: Within 30 days of receiving the order

steps.d: Pay excess funds to the identified shareholders under the scheme, or pass accounting entries to set off losses or adjust securities premium. A listed company fixes the record date with the exchanges and gives at least 7 working days' notice. Hold a board meeting or circular resolution to issue new share certificates for the reduced capital, cancel old ones, and file the corporate action for demat shares.
steps.time: Record date notice at least 7 working days

steps.d: If the reduction changes the Memorandum, alter it by special resolution at a general meeting and complete the formalities. A listed company sends the altered MOA to the exchanges.

resolutions.title: Special resolution for reduction of share capital
resolutions.text:
RESOLVED THAT, pursuant to Sections 66 and 52 and other applicable provisions of the Companies Act, 2013, the NCLT (Procedure for Reduction of Share Capital of Company) Rules, 2016 and the Articles of Association, and subject to the confirmation of the National Company Law Tribunal, the share capital of {co} be reduced from Rs. [existing capital] to Rs. [reduced capital] by [cancelling paid-up capital lost or not represented by assets / paying off paid-up capital in excess of the Company's needs / reducing liability on unpaid capital] as set out in the scheme.

RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the Board is authorised to accept any changes the NCLT or other authority requires and to do all acts needed.
resolutions.explanatory: The Company has [accumulated losses of Rs. [amount] / excess capital of Rs. [amount]] and proposes to reduce its share capital under Section 66. The proposed reduction, the effect on each class of shares, the valuation report of [name of valuer] and the accounting treatment are set out in the scheme open for inspection at the registered office. The reduction needs the confirmation of the NCLT after notice to creditors, the ROC, the Central Government and (for a listed company) SEBI. No director or KMP or their relatives is interested except as shareholders [state holdings]. The Board recommends the resolution.

resolutions.text:

RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the existing physical share certificates be cancelled on surrender, and the Company Secretary is authorised to file the corporate action with the depositories for demat shares.
RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the record date for the reduction be [date].

paras: To, [name of creditor], [address]. Subject: Application for reduction of share capital of {co}.

{co} has presented an application to the National Tribunal at [bench] to reduce its share capital from Rs. [existing] to Rs. [reduced]. Your name is entered in the list of creditors for a debt (or contingent debt or claim) of Rs. [amount].

If you wish to object or make a representation, send it to the Company within [time fixed by NCLT] of this notice. The list of creditors can be seen at the registered office on business days from [time] to [time].

docs.title: Advertisement for objections
paras: NOTICE. Before the National Company Law Tribunal, [bench]. Application no. [number] of {co}, CIN [CIN], registered office [address].

Notice is given that the Company has applied to reduce its share capital from Rs. [existing] to Rs. [reduced]. The list of creditors may be inspected at [place] on business days. Creditors may send objections to the Company within [period fixed by NCLT]. The matter will be heard on [date].

docs.title: Affidavit confirming dispatch and publication
paras: I, [name], Director of {co}, affirm that notices to the Central Government, the Registrar, [SEBI,] and the creditors were sent on [date], and that the notice was published in [English newspaper] and [vernacular newspaper] on [date] and uploaded to the Company's website.
Signed: [name]. Date: [date]. Place: [place].

flags: The reference note lists the auditor certificate on deposit arrears twice (items d and g of the NCLT filing list). It is the same document; attach it once.

Step 10 asks a company to file the board resolution in MGT-14. Section 179(3) filings under Section 117(3)(g) apply to public companies and a reduction of capital is not clearly a Section 179(3) matter. Check whether this filing is needed. The reference note marks it not applicable to private companies.
Listed company timings differ across the reference note (board outcome 30 minutes, general meeting 12 hours, NCLT outcome 24 hours). Confirm against the current Regulation 30 schedule.
The 3-month objection window and the 7-day deadlines are taken from the reference note; confirm against the 2016 NCLT Rules and any NCLT direction.

title: Accepting a loan or deposit
summary: Sets out how a company checks who is lending, gets board and member approval, signs the loan, records it and files the required forms.
when: When a company plans to borrow from directors, members, banks, other companies or the public.
applies: All companies; the Section 180(1)(c) limit applies to public companies; private companies have some deposit exemptions

steps.d: Find out whether the money comes from a director, a financial institution, a shareholder, another company or the public. Check the borrowing limits the company has.
Approve taking the loan, its terms and conditions, and other related matters. Authorise a director to take the follow-up steps.
If total borrowings would go beyond the aggregate of paid-up share capital, free reserves and securities premium, pass a special resolution of members under Section 180(1)(c).
The authorised director or officer of a public company files the special resolution passed under Section 180(1)(c) with the ROC.
The authorised director or officer signs the agreement with the lender for the company.
Enter the loan in the relevant statutory registers: register of deposits, register of contracts with related parties, register of charges, and any other that applies.
Show the loan in the notes to accounts. If it is from directors or related parties, disclose it in the Board's report as a related party transaction.
File the charge form if the lender takes security, and the deposit return, along with any other form that applies, within the prescribed limits.
Pay the principal and interest as the agreement requires.

A private company is also exempt from Section 180(1), though many follow it as good governance.

title: Holding the annual general meeting
summary: Takes the company from fixing the AGM due date through notice, e-voting, the meeting, minutes and post-meeting filings.
when: Every year, within the time limits in Section 96.
applies: All companies except One Person Companies. Private companies have some relief from provisions on notice, quorum and voting (see flags).

steps.d: The first AGM is due within 9 months of the end of the first financial year. Later AGMs are due within 6 months of the financial year end and not more than 15 months after the previous AGM.
Hold a board meeting under Section 173 and SS-1. Approve the date, time and venue or video conference link, the draft notice and agenda, and authorise a director or KMP to send the notice.

Prepare the notice under Section 101 and SS-2, listing ordinary and special business. Include proxy details, the website link, and the contact details of the grievance officer and compliance officer. Attach the explanatory statement (Section 102), the proxy form and ballot or poll details if relevant.
Send the notice to members, directors, auditors and debenture trustees by hand, post or electronic mode. Put it on the company website if there is one.
steps.time: At least 21 clear days before the AGM

steps.d: Complete the audited financial statements (Section 129), the Board's report (Section 134) and the auditor's report with annexures. Send them with the notice as Section 136 requires.
If Section 108 and Rule 20 apply, set up remote e-voting before the meeting and voting at the venue for members who have not voted remotely.
Check that the venue or video conference meets SS-2: seating, audio-video set-up, secure log-ins and a way to record proceedings.
Confirm the quorum (Section 103), elect or appoint the chairman if needed, take the agenda, let members ask questions, and take votes by show of hands, poll or electronic means.
Record the votes and declare whether each resolution is carried or lost, checking that the required majority was met.
File the annual return in MGT-7 (MGT-7A for small companies and OPCs), and MGT-14 for any special resolutions, within the prescribed times.
Write the minutes and enter them in the minutes book. The Chairman signs them.
Act on what was passed: director appointments or re-appointments, dividend, auditor appointment and so on.

title: Appointing a proxy for a general meeting
law: Section 105; Rule 19, Companies (Management and Administration) Rules, 2014
summary: Explains who can be a proxy, how the member appoints one, the deposit deadline, revocation and the proxy's rights.
when: When a member who can vote at a general meeting wants someone else to attend and vote.
applies: All companies; the reference note says private companies are exempt from Section 105 unless the Articles say otherwise

steps.d: Any member entitled to attend and vote may appoint a proxy. The proxy need not be a member.
One person may act as proxy for at most 50 members and for no more than 10% of the total share capital in all. A person holding more than 10% of the share capital can be proxy for one member only.
The proxy must be in writing, signed by the member or an authorised representative, in the prescribed form. A body corporate gives it under seal or signed by an authorised officer or attorney.
The form shows the member's details with the shares held, the proxy's details, the date, time and place of the meeting, the member's signature, the agenda and a revenue stamp.
Deposit it at the registered office. It may be sent by email or other electronic means only if the Articles permit.
steps.time: At least 48 hours before the meeting

steps.d: The member can revoke the proxy by written notice, or by attending and voting in person, which cancels the proxy.
The proxy may attend, speak and vote on a poll. The reference note says the proxy cannot vote on a show of hands unless the Articles allow it.
Members entitled to vote may inspect proxy forms during business hours, in the 24 hours before the meeting and until the meeting ends.
A member of a company registered under Section 8 may appoint only another member as proxy.

title: Passing a resolution by circulation
law: Sections 175, 179 and 180; Rules 5 and 8, Companies (Meetings of Board and its Powers) Rules, 2014; Secretarial Standards
summary: Gets board or committee approval by sending papers to each director in turn instead of holding a meeting.
when: When a matter needs board or committee approval but a meeting is not practical, and the matter is one the rules allow by circulation.
applies: All companies; there is no special exemption for private companies

steps.d: Send the draft resolution and supporting papers to every director, including any interested director, or to every committee member, at the same time and at the address registered with the company.
For each item, explain the proposal, the material facts needed to understand it, and any interest a director has. Include the draft resolution.
Tell directors how to give assent or dissent and by what date.
Send by hand, post, fax, email or other electronic means. Give each director seven days from the date of circulation to respond, and seek each director's decision separately for each resolution.
Preferably send one resolution per covering letter. If more than one goes in a letter, get each director's approval on each resolution separately.
The resolution passes when a majority of the directors entitled to vote, leaving out interested directors, approve it. A director who does not reply in time is treated as having abstained.
If the Articles need a special majority or the yes vote of named directors, the resolution passes only with that majority or vote.
If a director's interest has not yet been disclosed, the director discloses it and abstains.
If the required approval is not received by the last date, treat the resolution as not passed.

checklist: Matter is allowed to be passed by circulation
Draft resolution and papers sent to all directors at the same time
Note covers facts, interest of directors and how to respond
Last date for response set at least 7 days from circulation
Each resolution voted on separately
Interested directors left out of the count
Articles checked for special majority or named director
Result recorded and noted at the next board meeting

title: Re-appointing the retiring statutory auditor
law: Sections 139 and 141; Rules 3, 4 and 10, Companies (Audit and Auditors) Rules, 2014; Regulation 30, SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015
summary: Re-appoints the retiring auditor for a five-year term by board recommendation, ordinary resolution at the AGM, and filing of ADT-1.
when: When the term of the present auditor is ending or being renewed at an AGM.
applies: All companies; audit committee and stock exchange steps apply to listed companies and those required to have an audit committee

steps.d: Auditors hold office from one AGM to the conclusion of the sixth AGM after that. Listed companies, unlisted public companies with paid-up capital of Rs. 10 crore or more (excluding OPCs and small companies), private companies with Rs. 50 crore or more, and any company with public borrowings or deposits of Rs. 50 crore or more cannot appoint an individual for more than one five-year term, or a firm for more than two five-year terms. After the limit there is a five-year cooling off period.
For a listed entity, the auditor should hold an ICAI peer review certificate.
The audit committee, where one is required under Section 177, or otherwise the Board, considers the qualifications and experience of the auditor or firm.

Ask the auditor for written consent and a certificate showing eligibility under Section 141. It states that the auditor is eligible and not disqualified under the Act or the Chartered Accountants Act, that the appointment meets the term and limits in the Act, and that the list of pending professional conduct proceedings is true.
Where Section 177 applies or the company is listed, hold an audit committee meeting and recommend the name of the auditor.
Send notice to every director at the registered address by hand, post or electronic means. Attach the agenda, notes and draft resolution. Short notice is allowed in urgent cases.

Recommend the appointment or re-appointment for five years. Approve the AGM notice and explanatory statement. A listed company sends the outcome to the exchanges within the time the reference note gives (12 hours; see flags).

Give written or electronic notice of the AGM. Shorter notice needs the consent of a majority in number of members holding at least 95% of the voting paid-up capital. Send it to members, legal representatives of deceased members, assignees of insolvent members, the auditors and all directors. State the place, date, day and time and the business. For a listed company include the auditor fees, terms and basis of the recommendation and the auditor's credentials.

steps.t: Pass the resolution at the AGM
steps.d: Pass an ordinary resolution to appoint or re-appoint the auditor for five years and fix the remuneration.

steps.d: Send the proceedings to the exchanges (reference note: within 12 hours) and the voting results within 2 working days, and post both on the website. Telling the exchanges of the appointment is desirable. For the retiring auditor of a listed entity or its material subsidiaries, the SEBI circular of 18 October 2019 requires an auditor confirmation.

Tell the auditor about the appointment and file the notice with the Registrar. Attach a certified copy of the ordinary resolution, the appointment letter, the auditor's consent letter and the eligibility certificate.

title: Getting a Director Identification Number (DIN)
law: Section 153; Rule 9(1), Companies (Appointment and Qualification of Directors) Rules, 2014; Rule 10, Limited Liability Partnership Rules, 2009
summary: Explains the two ways to get a DIN, through SPICe+ Part B for a new company or through DIR-3 for an existing company, and the steps after allotment.
when: Before any individual can be appointed as a director of a company, or as a designated partner of an LLP.

steps.d: Use SPICe+ Part B if the person is to be a first director of a company being incorporated. Use DIR-3 if the person is to be appointed to an existing company.

File SPICe+ Part B on the MCA portal. A maximum of 3 DINs can be allotted through it. Attach proof of identity (PAN for Indian nationals, passport for foreign nationals), proof of address, a passport size photograph and a declaration in Form DIR-2. The DIN is allotted when the form is approved.
For an existing company, the Board approves the proposal to appoint the individual as a director, which is attached to the application.

Log in to the MCA portal and fill in Form DIR-3. Verify the mobile number and email by OTP. Enter the CIN, FCRN, LLPIN or FLLPIN of the entity where the applicant is to be a director or designated partner.

Attach a photograph, a self-attested PAN card (required for Indian nationals), a self-attested passport (required for foreign nationals), a self-attested identity proof (Aadhaar, passport, voter ID and so on), a self-attested residence proof (postpaid mobile bill, bank statement or utility bill) and the board resolution.

The applicant and an authorised director of the company in which the applicant is to be appointed both sign DIR-3 with their digital signature certificates. Upload the form on the MCA portal and pay the fee (currently Rs. 500).
MCA processes the form. On approval, the DIN is allotted and sent by email.
The director tells the company the DIN within 30 days using DIR-3B, where applicable. The company then informs the Registrar in DIR-12.
Each director files DIR-3 KYC every year by 30 September. A person may hold only one DIN. The DIN is valid for life unless it is deactivated, surrendered or cancelled.

The DIR-3 fee of Rs. 500 is as given; confirm the current schedule.

items: Any individual who is to be a director of a company must first get a Director Identification Number from the MCA.

New company: apply through Part B of SPICe+. Up to 3 DINs can be allotted this way. Attach proof of identity (PAN for Indians, passport for foreign nationals), proof of address, a passport-size photograph and the consent in Form DIR-2. The DIN is allotted when the SPICe+ is approved.

Existing company: file Form DIR-3 on the MCA portal with a photograph, a self-attested PAN (Indians) or passport (foreign nationals), a self-attested identity proof and address proof, and the Board resolution proposing the appointment. Verify the mobile number and e-mail by OTP, and give the CIN, FCRN, LLPIN or FLLPIN of the entity where the person is to be a director or partner.
DIR-3 must carry the digital signature of the applicant and of an authorised director of the company. Pay the fee (Rs. 500 at the time of writing). The DIN is e-mailed on approval.
The director tells the company of the DIN within 30 days in Form DIR-3B, where it applies.
The company then informs the Registrar in Form DIR-12.
One person can hold only one DIN. Holding more is an offence, with a penalty that may reach Rs. 50,000 and Rs. 500 for each day after.
A DIN is valid for life unless it is deactivated, surrendered or cancelled.
The director must file DIR-3 KYC every year by 30 September to keep the DIN active.

title: Moving the registered office from one State to another
law: Section 12 read with Rule 30, Companies (Incorporation) Rules, 2014
summary: Shifts the registered office to another State through board and member approval, creditor notice and Regional Director confirmation, and ends with a new certificate of incorporation.
when: When the company wants its registered office in a different State or Union Territory.
applies: All companies (private companies follow every step)

steps.d: Give in-principle approval for the shift to another State and ROC. Approve the change to the registered office clause of the Memorandum. Authorise directors or a person to sign papers and declarations and appear before the Regional Director. Call the extraordinary general meeting.
Pass a special resolution approving the shift to another State and ROC and the alteration of the registered office clause in the Memorandum, subject to the Regional Director's approval.
File the special resolution with the ROC.

steps.t: Fix the cut-off date and list creditors
steps.d: Choose a cut-off date for the list of creditors and debenture holders, on or after the EGM. Get a certificate for the list from the statutory auditor or a chartered accountant.

On the cut-off date, publish a notice in an English newspaper with wide circulation and a vernacular newspaper of the district. Send a copy of the advertisement to the Regional Director by registered post with acknowledgement due.

File the application with the Regional Director. Attach the altered MOA, the EGM papers, the board resolution or vakalatnama for appearance, the creditors' list, all declarations, the newspaper advertisements, proof of notices sent to the Chief Secretary, ROC, SEBI as relevant, the background to the shift, and MGT-14. Choose the cut-off date so that few or no creditors are owed on that date.
steps.time: Within 1 month of the cut-off date

steps.d: Send each creditor a letter with a format for a no objection to the shift.

Send the application and supporting documents to the Chief Secretary of the State or Union Territory and to the ROC by registered post with acknowledgement due. File the application or notice with the ROC. Send the original application to the Regional Director's office.

If creditors object, the Regional Director holds a hearing and may ask the company to file an affidavit recording what was agreed. With no objection, the application goes up for an order. Follow up with the office, and give any extra papers asked for.
When the Regional Director's order arrives, file it with the ROC.
steps.time: Within 30 days of receiving the order

steps.t: Board resolution on the exact address
steps.d: After INC-28 is approved, pass a board resolution to shift the registered office to the exact address.

steps.t: File notice of the new address
steps.d: File notice of the new registered office with the ROC.
On approval of INC-22, the revised certificate of incorporation with the new CIN is received. The shift takes effect from the date of that certificate.

title: Changing the object clause of the Memorandum
law: Section 13; Rule 24, Companies (Management and Administration) Rules, 2014 (as cited in the reference note); Regulations 30, 44 and 46(3), SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015
summary: Changes the objects in the Memorandum by board approval, a special resolution of members and filing with the Registrar.
when: When the company wants to add to, drop or change its objects.
applies: All companies; extra stock exchange steps for listed companies

steps.d: Pass a board resolution approving the proposed change to the object clause and the notice of the extraordinary general meeting with an explanatory statement under Section 102.
Send the notice to all shareholders and directors, unless shorter notice is consented to by the required majority.
steps.time: At least 21 days before the meeting

steps.d: Pass a special resolution under Section 13(1) to alter the object clause.
File the form with a certified copy of the special resolution, the EGM notice with explanatory statement, the altered MOA and the board resolution.
steps.time: Within 30 days of the special resolution

steps.d: Tell the stock exchanges the outcome of the board meeting within the time the reference note gives (24 hours; see flags). Post it on the website within 2 working days.
Send the proceedings of the general meeting to the exchanges within 24 hours of the close and post them within 2 working days. Send the voting results within 2 working days of the meeting.
After MGT-14 is filed and the ROC approves, send a copy of the altered MOA to the exchanges within 24 hours of the event and post it on the website within 2 working days.

The reference note does not mention Section 13(8). If the company raised money from the public by a prospectus and has not used it, shareholders who dissent must be offered an exit, and there are extra requirements. Check this.

Section 22(16) of the postal ballot rules (Rule 22(16) of the Management and Administration Rules) may require this resolution to be passed by postal ballot, or by e-voting if the company offers it. Check.

title: Issuing bonus shares
law: Section 63; Companies (Share Capital and Debentures) Rules, 2014; for listed companies, SEBI (ICDR) Regulations, 2018
summary: Allots fully paid-up shares free to existing members in proportion to their holding, paid for from free reserves, securities premium or the capital redemption reserve.
when: When a company wants to capitalise reserves and give existing members extra shares.
applies: All companies; some general meeting and demat steps differ for private companies (see flags)

steps.d: See that the Articles allow the issue of bonus shares. If not, pass a special resolution to alter them.

Hold the meeting under Section 173 and SS-1. Approve the bonus proposal, the number and ratio of bonus shares and the record date. Authorise the company secretary or another officer to send the general meeting notice, circulate the minutes and take the other steps needed.

If authorised capital must go up, or if members must approve, hold a general meeting. Pass an ordinary resolution for the bonus issue, and a special resolution to alter the Memorandum if authorised capital is to be increased.
File a copy of the board resolution and the special resolution with the Registrar with the documents and fee.
The Board allots fully paid-up bonus shares to eligible members in proportion to their holdings on the record date.
Attach the general meeting resolution authorising the bonus issue, the board resolution for allotment, the list of allottees and any other mandatory attachment.
For physical shares, issue certificates in Form SH-1. For shares dealt in a depository, tell the depository about the allotment immediately. Pay stamp duty under the Stamp Act on each certificate.
Enter each certificate's particulars in the register of members with the name of the holder and the date of issue.

The Company has not defaulted on interest or principal of deposits or debt securities or on statutory dues of employees. flags: The reference note says private companies may approve a bonus issue by board resolution alone if the Articles allow. Section 63(2) needs authority in the Articles and authority from members in a general meeting on the Board's recommendation, with no carve-out for private companies. Check before skipping the general meeting.

The reference note does not list the Section 63 conditions: no bonus from revaluation reserves; no default on deposits, debt securities or statutory employee dues; partly paid shares to be made fully paid first. Add these checks.

The reference note does not give the SEBI ICDR timelines for listed companies (bonus to be implemented within 15 days of board approval if no member approval is needed, otherwise within 2 months of the board meeting). Check the current regulations.

The reference note says a special resolution is needed to alter the MOA for an increase of capital. Section 61(1)(a) allows an increase by ordinary resolution if the Articles allow, and SH-7 is to be filed within 30 days; the reference note omits SH-7. A special resolution is the safe course.
Bonus shares cannot be issued in lieu of dividend (Section 63(3)); check the current text.
private: A private company need not hold a general meeting for a bonus issue if its Articles let the Board do it. A Board resolution is enough. If the Articles do not allow it, alter them first by special resolution. A private company with shares in physical form can issue physical certificates and has no duty to credit bonus shares to demat accounts.
